[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Coachella < Spanish 'coachella' (from Coachella Valley, but as sound: 'coche' (car) + '-ella' (diminutive); Latin 'cocca' = berry, seed",
    "reading": "A small vehicle or seed; the diminutive of a shell or husk, a pod that carries.",
    "languages": ["es", "la"],
    "source": "Diccionario de la lengua española (RAE), Lewis & Short Latin Dictionary",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "coach + ella; coach (English) = carriage, instruction; ella (Spanish) = she",
    "reading": "She who instructs; the feminine guide in a carriage, a moving lesson.",
    "languages": ["en", "es"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.7
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "coach (en) ~ 'coche' (fr) = shell, husk; 'ella' (es) = she; 'cocher' (fr) = to cook, to ripen",
    "reading": "The ripening shell that cooks within; a feminine husk maturing into fruit.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr", "es"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Coachella → 'chela' (claw, pincer) + 'coa' (cocoa, or 'coa' = ancient Egyptian basket)",
    "reading": "A clawed basket; a grasping vessel that holds what is offered.",
    "languages": ["en", "grc", "egy"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "C-O-A-C-H-E-L-L-A → C(hrist) O(mnium) A(nnorum) C(ustos) H(ominum) E(terna) L(ux) L(ux) A(eterna)",
    "reading": "Christ, guardian of all years, eternal light for humanity; a luminous keeper.",
    "languages": ["la"],
    "source": "generative (notariqon tradition)",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "C = 100, O = 0, A = 1, C = 100, H = 8, E = 5, L = 50, L = 50, A = 1; sum = 315; 3+1+5 = 9",
    "reading": "The number nine: completion, the end of a cycle, the threshold of return.",
    "languages": ["la", "grc"],
    "source": "generative (gematria, isopsephy)",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "coa + chella; 'coa' (Nahuatl) = serpent; 'chella' (Arabic) = desert plain",
    "reading": "A serpent in the desert; the winding path across barren ground.",
    "languages": ["nah", "ar"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Coachella < Cahuilla (Native American tribe) via Spanish 'coachella' — but as sound: 'cahuilla' = 'place of the water' (from Cahuilla language)",
    "reading": "A place of water; a basin where life gathers, though the name sounds of a shell.",
    "languages": ["cahuilla", "es"],
    "source": "Cahuilla dictionary (Bright, 1968)",
    "confidence": 0.4
  }
]
